title: EPIC 15: Round-2 Dual-Pass Code Review (2026-07-18)
description:
BACKGROUND: On 2026-07-17, all 19 Lua source files were written/modified in a single burst (~22:28-22:37 UTC) as part of the PRD-compliance implementation push (Epics 1-9). The next session was wiped by a daily reset, so the review had to reconstruct 'what was just written' from file mtimes before it could review anything.

METHODOLOGY: A dual-pass review was executed per the ultrathink-analysis skill's recommended pattern for >5-file reviews:
  1. PARENT PASS — Full read of every file by the primary reviewer, tracing cross-references and checking against the PRD.
  2. SUBAGENT PASS — An independent background audit subagent read all 19 files with the distilled server-authority-gap-checklist (11 exploit/bug classes from the Harbor Heist round-1 review).
  3. RECONCILIATION — ~60% overlap confirmed findings; ~40% were unique to one pass.

RESULTS: 13 bugs found and fixed, 2 design decisions flagged for user input, 4 new bug classes added to the skill's checklist. All fixes syntax-verified via `luau` compiler.

This epic tracks ALL findings from that session — both the fixed bugs (for record-keeping and regression-prevention) and the two design decisions that need user input. Each bug bead links to the relevant existing EPIC 14 task where one exists.

WHY THIS EPIC EXISTS: The existing EPIC 14 (Post-Review Hardening) was created from the round-1 review. This epic captures the round-2 findings, many of which are NEW bug classes (raw-parameter deref, client-server kind mismatch, cosmetic-field-on-nonexistent-session, advertised-multiplier-never-applied) that round-1's checklist didn't cover. The skill's reference file (server-authority-gap-checklist.md) was extended with entries #12-15 to capture these.

CONSIDERATIONS:
- 3 bugs were CRITICAL (would crash or silently break core gameplay on first use)
- 5 bugs were HIGH (features non-functional, progression broken)
- The subagent found 2 issues the parent pass missed (TOCTOU steal, dead code)
- 4 new bug classes were distilled and added to the permanent checklist
- Two items were flagged as DESIGN DECISIONS (not bugs): the dead CastResult remote and the brutal honest-client catch rate. These became EPIC 16 and a task in EPIC 6 respectively.
close_reason: All 10 bug children fixed + closed. Review complete; record retained in descriptions. 4 new bug classes (#12-15) added to ultrathink-analysis/server-authority-gap-checklist.md.

title: BUG 15.1 [FIXED]: DataManager nil-deref on first join (data.dailyQuestKey)
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — 100% reproducible crash on EVERY new player's first join.

ROOT CAUSE: DataManager.load() (line 335) read `data.dailyQuestKey` from the raw saved-data parameter, but `data` is nil for brand-new players (no DataStore entry) or when the datastore load fails. Indexing nil throws "attempt to index nil with 'dailyQuestKey'", crashing the session initialization.

WHY IT WAS MISSED: The sanitize() call above it (`local profile = sanitize(saved)`) looks like it handles everything, so the later `data.dailyQuestKey` reads seem safe. But `data` is the original function parameter, not the sanitized output. This only crashes on first join or datastore failure — easy to miss in testing if you always have existing save data.

FIX APPLIED (N2): Read from `profile.dailyQuestKey` (the sanitized result, guaranteed non-nil) instead of `data.dailyQuestKey`.

This is a NEW bug class (#12 in the server-authority-gap-checklist): raw-parameter dereference in load functions. Added to the skill's permanent checklist.

title: BUG 15.2 [FIXED]: Legacy liveWell migration overwritten by unconditional sanitizeStoredFish(nil)
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — silent total fish loss for v1 saves with a partial Aquarium table.

ROOT CAUSE: In DataManager.sanitize(), line 146 ran `clean.Aquarium.StoredFish = sanitizeStoredFish(aq.StoredFish)` UNCONDITIONALLY. When `aq.StoredFish` is nil (a v1 save with only `liveWell`), `sanitizeStoredFish(nil)` returns `{}`, overwriting the fish just migrated from `liveWell` at line 107.

The round-1 review (EPIC 14, TASK 14.2) identified this class and added a "fix" at line 172, but the guard was in the WRONG PLACE — it re-ran sanitizeStoredFish when `aq.StoredFish` WAS a table (redundant), instead of guarding line 146 where the actual clobbering happened.

FIX APPLIED (N3): Made line 146 conditional (`if type(aq.StoredFish) == "table" then`). Removed the redundant line-172 block.

This is checklist item #3 (Legacy Migration Overwrite) — the same class as round-1, but the round-1 fix was incomplete. The lesson: when adding a guard, verify it guards the ACTUAL overwrite site, not a redundant re-execution.

title: BUG 15.3 [FIXED]: Quest rewards never credited — session.cash does not exist
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — quest completion shows "+$X" toast but credits ZERO coins, AND errors silently ("arithmetic on nil value").

ROOT CAUSE: QuestService.processList (line 87) wrote `session.cash += q.reward`. The session object (DataManager.lua:311-339) has no `cash` field — money lives at `session.profile.Coins`. The `session.cash +=` operation creates a new transient field that is never read by anything and never persisted. Worse, `+=` on nil errors with "attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value" inside the quest loop.

FIX APPLIED (N4): Replaced with:
  session.profile.Coins = PlayerProfile.clampCoins(session.profile.Coins + q.reward)
  session.profile.TotalCoinsEarned = session.profile.TotalCoinsEarned + q.reward

This routes through clampCoins (matching every other coin-grant path) and tracks lifetime earnings. Added `require(PlayerProfile)` import to QuestService.

IMPACT: Every daily and weekly quest (11 templates, 3 daily + 2 weekly slots) was silently broken. Players could see the completion notification but received no reward. The error happened inside a loop in a potentially task.spawn'd context, so it may have silently broken ALL quest progression (not just the completing quest).

title: BUG 15.4 [FIXED]: Lock/Alarm/Capacity upgrade system non-functional (5-file chain broken)
description:
SEVERITY: HIGH — 3 of 5 shop upgrade categories were unbuyable AND non-functional even if purchased.

ROOT CAUSE: A 5-file chain of broken connections:
  1. PlayerProfile.default() had NO LockLevel/AlarmLevel fields (sanitize dropped them)
  2. DataManager.sanitize() wrote them to top-level `clean.lockLevel` (orphan fields, not in schema)
  3. ShopService.BuyItem returned `bad_kind` for "lock"/"alarm" (only handled rod/bait/aquarium)
  4. Client sent kind="capacity" but server only accepted "aquarium" (kind mismatch)
  5. Client built shop rows from GameConfig.Upgrades.Capacity (3 entries) but server sold from GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers (4 entries, different prices)
  6. AquariumService read `victimSession.alarmLevel` (nonexistent session field) — alarms never triggered
  7. AquariumService lock-duration scaling was a stub (`if UpgradeLevel > 1 then -- future`)
  8. StateSync.snapshot didn't expose any upgrade levels — client always saw 0
  9. RodService.read `session.rodLevel` (nonexistent) — rod visual always level 1

FIX APPLIED (N5-N10):
  - Added LockLevel, AlarmLevel to PlayerProfile.Aquarium schema
  - Sanitize persists them in the nested Aquarium table + maps legacy top-level fields
  - ShopService handles "lock", "alarm" kinds with proper catalog + currentLevel dispatch
  - Client sends "aquarium" (not "capacity") and uses AquariumUpgradeTiers catalog
  - Client KIND_META and refreshShop use "aquarium" key consistently
  - AquariumService.handleSteal reads profile.Aquarium.AlarmLevel
  - AquariumService.LockAquarium scales duration/cooldown from Upgrades.Lock[lockLevel]
  - StateSync.snapshot exposes upgradeLevel, lockLevel, alarmLevel
  - RodService reads profile.Equipment.EquippedRodLevel
  - Removed dead KIND_CATALOGS/getCatalog from ShopService

This is checklist item #13 (Client-Server Kind/String Mismatch) and #14 (Cosmetic Field On Nonexistent Session Attribute). Both added to the permanent checklist.

title: BUG 15.5 [FIXED]: onFishCaught quest hook never called + rarity type mismatch
description:
SEVERITY: HIGH — 3 of 11 quest templates (catch_rarity) could never progress.

ROOT CAUSE: QuestService.onFishCaught(session, rarityIndex) was defined but never called anywhere. Even if it HAD been called, it expected a numeric rarity index, but FishInstance.Rarity is a STRING ("Common", "Rare", etc.). The comparison `rarityIndex >= (q.rarity or 1)` with a string on the left and number on the right would error in Luau.

FIX APPLIED (N11):
  1. FishingService.SubmitCatchInput now calls `questService.onFishCaught(session, fish.Rarity)` after a successful catch
  2. QuestService.onFishCaught now accepts either a string or number, normalizing via a RARITY_ORDINAL lookup table: {Common=1, Uncommon=2, Rare=3, Epic=4, Legendary=5}

IMPACT: "Catch 5 Rare+", "Catch 3 Epic+", "Catch a Legendary" quests were all dead. Now they progress on every catch that meets the rarity threshold.

title: BUG 15.6 [FIXED]: Unclamped coin write on steal-fence (AquariumService:282)
description:
SEVERITY: HIGH — the ONLY coin-granting path in the codebase that bypassed clampCoins.

ROOT CAUSE: When an attacker's aquarium is full and they fence a stolen fish for coins, AquariumService.handleSteal did `attackerSession.profile.Coins = attackerSession.profile.Coins + stolenFish.BaseSellValue` — raw write, no clamp, no TotalCoinsEarned update.

EXPLOIT: Near the MAX_COINS ceiling (999,999,999), a large fencing payout could overflow past the cap. Also, a crafted/hijacked BaseSellValue (if sanitize regressed) could go negative — this was the one path that wouldn't clamp to >= 0.

FIX APPLIED (N12): Route through PlayerProfile.clampCoins + update TotalCoinsEarned.

This is checklist item #9 (Unclamped Economy Writes). The round-1 review caught most sites; this one was added later (the steal-fence path) and missed the clamp.

title: BUG 15.7 [FIXED]: AquariumUpgradeTiers.incomeMultiplier advertised but never applied

title: BUG 15.9 [FIXED]: TOCTOU race in steal resolution — stale index could steal raid-protected fish
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL (latent) — raid-protected Legendary fish could be stolen despite IsRaidProtected check.

FOUND BY: Background audit subagent (C6 in its report). The parent pass missed this because the race window is currently safe (single-threaded Luau, no yields between eligibility check and table.remove). But the code is FRAGILE — any future refactor that adds a yield (task.spawn, remote call) between snapshot and remove would make it exploitable.

ROOT CAUSE: handleSteal builds an `eligible` list of INDICES (positions in victimFish) for non-raid-protected fish. After the rng roll picks `stolenIndex = eligible[N]`, `table.remove(victimFish, stolenIndex)` removes at that index. If the victim sold/stored a fish between the eligibility snapshot and the remove (via a concurrent SellAll or StoreSingleFish), the indices shift, and `table.remove(victimFish, 3)` could now point at a DIFFERENT fish — possibly a raid-protected Legendary.

FIX APPLIED (N15): Capture the fish REFERENCE (not index) at selection time. Re-find it in the live list via identity comparison (`fish == targetFish`), re-validate `not fish.IsRaidProtected`, then remove. If the target vanished or became protected, fail-safe as a miss rather than stealing the wrong fish.

title: EPIC 10: Security & Anti-Exploit Hardening
description:
PRD security/anti-exploit section (lines 477-484). The current code already has good server-authoritative patterns (nil guards, bounds checks, capacity re-checks, distance validation). This epic formalizes it into an AntiExploitService + adds rate limiting, suspicious-action tracking, and audit logging.

WHY P0: exploits destroy game economies and trust. PRD: 'No client can change currency, rarity, inventory, or raid result.' All valuable transactions server-confirmed.

## BACKGROUND & JUSTIFICATION
Part of the Harbor Heist V1 build — migrating the current prototype to full PRD compliance (see PRD.md). The current codebase is a working server-authoritative prototype with 5 rarity tiers, basic cast/store/sell, passive income, and basic theft/lock PvP. The PRD demands a richer experience: structured data, 12-20 species, timing minigame, claimable income, collection book, upgrade tree, scheduled opt-in raids, onboarding, analytics, and anti-exploit. Every bead serves the overarching goal: a cozy fishing-aquarium game with optional bounded PvP heists that creates social stories without griefing.

## PRD TRACEABILITY
See PRD.md for the authoritative spec. PRD requirement IDs (e.g. FISH-01, AQUA-03, PVP-05) are referenced in task acceptance criteria.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] All remotes rate-limited
- [ ] Suspicious actions logged
- [ ] No dup/negative/exploit path exists
- [ ] Raid transfers atomic
- [ ] Failure handling user-visible

title: EPIC 20: UI/UX Audit Remediation — Player-Facing Polish & Core-Loop Repair
description:
Umbrella epic for the 2026-07-23 fresh-eyes UI/UX audit of the entire player-facing experience.

## Origin & method
A full manual audit read every line of the client UI (src/client/init.client.lua, 3042 lines), the shared UI-driving config (GameConfig, FishDefinitions, ZoneDefinitions, FishVisuals), and the server services whose contracts the UI renders (Fishing, Aquarium, Raid, Shop, Quest, Collection, StateSync, DockManager, init.server). Git history/blame was used to separate regressions from long-standing issues and to confirm suspected bugs against server contracts rather than guessing.

## Findings (17 total)
- CRITICAL (2): bite minigame never starts (BiteEvent arity regression — fishing is unplayable); desktop action bar clips on <=768px-wide viewports.
- HIGH (6): FISH button has no lifecycle states; cast-while-casting is silent; HUD income shows +$0.0/sec all early game; catch success is a vertically-clipped toast; three minigame overlays stack uncoordinated on the same screen position; claimable income invisible from the HUD.
- MEDIUM (9): SELL ALL liquidates tank+bag unconfirmed; lock status absent from raid targets; raid targets never auto-refresh; lock button copy leaks implementation detail; onboarding prompt hardcoded offset can collide on small mobile screens; collection book uses placeholder F/? icons; no inventory sorting; no persistent cast-zone guidance; minor polish (first-join cash count-up, unbounded toast stack, unreadable raid hint text, unclamped desktop panels).

## Sequencing rationale
1. EPIC 21 first: the P0 core-loop regression blocks play AND blocks verification of every other fishing-flow improvement.
2. EPICs 22-24 next: the feedback layers (cast lifecycle, overlay arbitration, HUD economy visibility) are what make the loop feel alive — these map directly to the PRD UX principles (immediate fishing feedback; always-visible Coins/capacity/claimable income).
3. EPICs 25-26: safety and clarity (unconfirmed SELL ALL is a rage-quit vector; raid panel transparency is a PRD PVP-04 requirement).
4. EPICs 27-29: polish and discoverability — the difference between functional and premium.

## Non-goals for this umbrella
- No visual rebrand: keep the existing design-token system (UI palette, Gotham font scale, EASE_* tweens) — it is already consistent and good.
- No new gameplay features beyond what findings require.
- Preserve the rebuild-guard signature patterns (inventory/collection lists) and the server-authoritative contracts; UI work must not weaken anti-exploit boundaries.

## PRD alignment
PRD First five minutes requires catch -> store -> earn -> upgrade inside the opening session and time-to-first-catch under 2 minutes. Finding 1 makes that impossible today; findings 3-8 are the difference between a funnel that retains and one that leaks at every step.

title: EPIC 21: P0 Core-Loop Repair — Bite Minigame Regression
description:
THE core-loop-breaking bug from the audit (finding 1). Fishing is currently unplayable end-to-end.

## What is broken
The server fires the bite with TWO arguments (FishingService.lua:213): remotes.BiteEvent:FireClient(player, zoneId, BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS). The client handler declares ONE parameter (init.client.lua:3003): Remotes.BiteEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(windowSeconds) ...). windowSeconds therefore receives the zoneId STRING ("StarterPier"). runMinigame assigns minigameWindow = that string, and the first frame of the sweep loop hits `elapsed > minigameWindow` -> runtime error "attempt to compare number < string" -> the spawned loop dies instantly, the FISH ON! minigame frame never becomes visible, and every bite times out server-side (SubmitCatchInput is never invoked by the player).

## Git forensics (verified via blame, not speculation)
- 869d93a (fishing rework) had the CORRECT two-arg signature: function(zoneId, windowSeconds).
- d5505ac ("client UI nil-safety + cleanup") collapsed the handler to one arg AND dropped the minigameWindow local.
- 2c07147 ("Fix client UI regressions from d5505ac") restored the minigameWindow local but MISSED the handler signature — so the regression shipped.
Lesson for future self: when a cleanup commit touches remote handlers, diff the handler arity against every FireClient call site. Arity drift between FireClient args and handler params fails SILENTLY in Luau until a value is used in a typed operation.

## Why P0 above everything
PRD success metrics (time-to-first-cast < 60s, time-to-first-catch < 2 min, first-session funnel) are unachievable. Every fishing-flow UX improvement in EPICs 22-23 cannot even be verified until this lands. Nothing else in this umbrella should start before TASK 21.1.

## Scope
Fix the signature, add a regression guard so this class of bug is caught mechanically next time, and leave a manual verification runbook for the catch flow.

title: TASK 21.1: Fix BiteEvent client handler signature (one-line P0 fix)
description:
Restore the two-argument BiteEvent handler so the bite minigame actually runs.

## The fix
init.client.lua:3003 — change:
    Remotes.BiteEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(windowSeconds)
to:
    Remotes.BiteEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(zoneId, windowSeconds)
Server contract (FishingService.lua:213): FireClient(player, zoneId, BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS). Keep the zoneId parameter NAMED (not _) even though it is unused today — it documents the wire contract and enables future zone-specific presentation. This is exactly what the original rework commit 869d93a had.

## TRUE failure signature (corrected 2026-07-23 plan-space review)
The original bead text said the frame "never appears" — wrong. runMinigame sets minigameFrame.Visible = true BEFORE the sweep loop starts (init.client.lua:2646), so the FISH ON! frame DOES appear — frozen. The marker never moves (stuck at x=0, outside the zone), the loop dies on its first comparison (number > string), so: no timeout expiry, minigameActive stays true (blocking ALL future bites via the early return at 2642), and any tap on the frozen frame submits markerPos=0 -> hit=false -> guaranteed miss. The symptom a tester sees: "the FISH ON! box pops up but the marker never moves and every catch fails" — sticky across casts. This is why the acceptance criteria below require a MOVING marker; a visible frame alone proves nothing.

## Also in scope (same class of bug, cheap to verify while here)
Walk every Remotes.*.OnClientEvent handler in init.client.lua and diff its parameter list against the matching server FireClient call site: StateChanged (1 arg), Notify (2 args), RaidWindowChanged (3 args, verified vs RaidService.lua:760), CastState (3 args; the (false, 0) / (false, 0, nil) fires are handled by the else branch), BiteEvent (2 args), OpenAquarium/OpenShop (0 args), QuestProgressChanged (1 arg). The audit already checked these and found BiteEvent to be the only mismatch — record the re-verification result in a closing comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bite minigame frame appears AND the marker VISIBLY SWEEPS back and forth (a frozen frame is the bug, not the fix)
- [ ] Tapping with the marker inside the zone catches a fish end-to-end in Studio play-solo (fish lands in bag)
- [ ] Letting the minigame time out hides the frame and notifies (loop alive)
- [ ] No "attempt to compare" errors in client log
- [ ] Handler-arity walk documented in a closing comment
close_reason: Fix landed in commit e5c7295 (BiteEvent handler arity: function(zoneId, windowSeconds)). Handler-arity walk completed by DarkElk; regression guard in hvfh.1.2 (commit b1a51ab). Runtime verification runbook is TASK 21.3 (separate bead). Marking closed — code is committed and in the tree; stale in_progress status corrected by RainyLynx.

title: TASK 21.2: Regression guard for remote-payload shape (BiteEvent + handler arity)
description:
Make this CLASS of bug fail loudly next time instead of silently killing the core loop.

## Why this task exists
The P0 regression survived TWO code reviews (d5505ac introduced it, 2c07147 partially fixed the same commit and still missed it) because nothing mechanical checks that client handler arity matches server FireClient arguments. Luau binds extra args to nil and missing args positionally; the failure only manifests at runtime when a mistyped value hits a typed operation. That is too late.

## PRIMARY deliverable: static arity contract check (decided in plan-space review 2026-07-23)
A small script (pure runner or CI shell step) that:
1. ast-grep/rg every server-side FireClient/FireAllClients call per remote name and counts payload arguments (excluding the player arg).
2. ast-grep/rg every client OnClientEvent:Connect(function(...) handler and counts declared params.
3. Fails the build on any mismatch where a client handler declares FEWER params than the server sends (more params is safe — they bind nil).
Source of truth for the pairing: Remotes.lua EVENT_NAMES + the client Remotes folder enumeration (init.client.lua:12-15). Runs in the existing CI pipeline alongside TestEZ — deterministic, no game instance needed, catches the drift at lint time.

## STRETCH (only if EPIC 19 harness reaches client UI state)
E2E case: fire a synthetic BiteEvent with the real payload shape and assert the minigame frame becomes Visible AND marker.Position changes within N seconds. Higher fidelity but depends on harness capabilities that are still being built (harborheist-pe9a). Do NOT block this bead on the harness — the static check ships regardless. Coordinate with pe9a owners before adding e2e surface (related link exists).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Static check fails when the BiteEvent handler arity is wrong (prove by reverting the fix locally, watch it fail, restore)
- [ ] Check runs in the standard quality gate alongside existing suites
- [ ] Closing comment records which remotes are covered

title: TASK 21.3: Manual verification runbook for the full catch flow
description:
A repeatable Studio play-solo script that proves the core loop works and serves as the verification baseline for EPIC 22/23 work.

## Content (each step: action -> expected UI)
1. Join -> welcome toast within ~5s; onboarding banner points at the zone.
2. Press F in the glowing zone -> cast overlay appears, marker sweeps, zone bands visible.
3. Click in the good/perfect band -> tier toast (PERFECT CAST / Good cast).
4. Wait for bite -> FISH ON! minigame appears AND THE MARKER VISIBLY SWEEPS (a frozen frame with a static marker is the 21.1 regression signature — fail immediately if seen).
5. Tap with the marker in the zone -> catch toast + fish appears in bag; sell-vs-store comparison prompt on FIRST catch.
6. Press G -> bag lists the fish with species/rarity/value and working SELL/STORE buttons.
7. STORE -> fish appears in aquarium; income/sec label updates (note: known issue TASK 22.3 — early-game rates read +$0.0/sec until that bead lands); capacity bar moves.
8. Claim -> balance animates up; gain floater appears.

## Where it lives
Append the runbook results as a comment on this bead (self-contained: the bead IS the runbook). If the e2e suite (EPIC 19) later automates client-side assertions, this runbook is the spec it encodes — that is the long-term intent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Runbook executed fresh after the 21.1 fix with all 8 steps passing
- [ ] Actual results recorded in a closing comment (including any steps that exposed NEW issues, filed as follow-ups)

title: EPIC 22: Fishing Feedback & Cast Lifecycle UX
description:
Audit findings 3, 4, 5, 6: the cast-to-catch lifecycle is a 6-10 second black box and its emotional payoff is a clipped toast.

## Background
- The FISH button distinguishes only casting true/false (init.client.lua:2392-2398), and `casting` spans the ENTIRE bite wait (rod castTime 2-4s + random 2-6s, FishingService.lua:109-110). No waiting-for-bite state, no cooldown feedback, no bite-ready state.
- doFish (init.client.lua:2736) silently returns when casting — the button feels dead exactly when the player is most tempted to press it.
- incomeLabel renders +$%.1f/sec (init.client.lua:2382) — a starter tank at 2 coins/min displays +$0.0/sec for the whole early game, hiding that the aquarium earns anything.
- A catch (even Legendary) is a single top-toast line; server strings like "You caught a Legendary Abyssal Eel! (worth $500)" (FishingService.lua:454) wrap to 2 lines in a fixed 40-42px toast with TextWrapped=true and clip vertically. PRD explicitly requires "cast cue, bite cue, timing feedback, catch reveal, and rarity presentation".

## Why it matters
This is the retention core: the PRD first-session funnel depends on the loop FEELING responsive and rewarding. The game currently hides its two biggest dopamine beats (a bite arriving, a rare catch landing) behind silence and a clipped toast.

## Design intent for future self
Server already pushes the edges we need (CastState true/false at FishingService.lua:144/187; structured catch result from SubmitCatchInput returning { ok, speciesId, rarity, value } at FishingService.lua:457). All fixes are client-side presentation; do NOT add new remotes, and do NOT re-derive economy values client-side (R2.2/dt9.2 lesson: StateSync snapshot is the single source of truth).

title: TASK 22.1: FISH button lifecycle states (idle / waiting / bite-ready)
description:
Give the primary action button a real state machine instead of a binary casting flag.

## Current behavior
render() (init.client.lua:2392-2398) shows "CASTING"/"..." greyed whenever the casting flag is true — and that flag spans the ENTIRE 6-10s bite wait. There is no visual difference between "cast flying", "waiting for a bite", and "A FISH IS BITING".

## Target states and EXACT transition edges (verified against server event order)
- idle -> waiting-for-bite: on CastState(true). Subtle animated state, e.g. "WAITING…" with a slow stroke pulse.
- waiting -> idle: on CastState(false) with no bite (cast cancelled / left zone / hands full).
- waiting -> bite-ready: CastState(false) fires FIRST then BiteEvent fires (verified: FishingService.lua:187 precedes :213 in the same deferred callback). So: on BiteEvent, enter bite-ready REGARDLESS of the flag state. "FISH ON!" in the warn accent.
- bite-ready -> idle: when the LOCAL minigame closes (tap or timeout — onMinigameTap / the expiry path in runMinigame). NOT on any CastState event; none is coming.

## Explicitly descoped (plan-space review 2026-07-23)
The original draft included a "rejected/cooldown red flash" state. REMOVED: cast rejections (hands full / wrong zone / rate-limited) reach the client ONLY as Notify toasts — RequestCast is a RemoteEvent with no return value, so there is no rejection signal to drive a button state. Options were a new remote (scope creep, server change for a nicety) or string-matching Notify text (fragile — violates the same no-string-parsing principle documented on TASK 22.4). The server toast IS the rejection feedback; the button does not need to mirror it.

## Constraints
- No new remotes: CastState and BiteEvent already provide every edge needed.
- Single state variable, transitions only on server events — never per-frame text churn in render().
- Mobile parity: the mobile stack shows the action key + short label (init.client.lua:2178-2193); the state must read on a 60px round button (color/pulse, not just text).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All three states visually distinct on desktop AND mobile
- [ ] bite-ready survives the CastState(false)-before-BiteEvent ordering (state test documented)
- [ ] No toast duplication with server notifications
close_reason: Implemented FISH button state machine (idle/waiting/bite-ready); headless-verified (tests 100/0/0, arity 8/8, selene zero-new, isolated lune logic pass). Visual acceptance (3 distinct states on desktop+mobile, pulse animates) deferred to EPIC 19 E2E / Studio play-solo per the 21.1/21.3 pattern.

title: TASK 22.2: Cast-while-casting feedback (button never feels dead)
description:
doFish (init.client.lua:2736) silently returns when casting is true. During a 6-10s bite wait the player WILL press F again — today nothing happens and the button reads as broken.

## Target behavior
On a cast attempt while waiting: lightweight negative feedback — a short button shake (2-3 frame offset tween) OR a rate-limited micro-toast "Waiting for a bite…" (max once per ~2s so spam-clicking does not flood the toast stack). Prefer the shake: it is instant, local, and adds zero toast pressure. Reuse pressFeedback tween patterns already in the file (init.client.lua:125-142).

## Why not a server round-trip
The rejection is knowable client-side (casting flag is local truth between CastState edges). Adding server chatter for a purely local UX nicety would be wasteful and lag-prone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Repeat-pressing F during a bite wait produces immediate visible feedback every press (or rate-limited if toast)
- [ ] No interference with the bite minigame input handling

Proof: test/_hvfh_2_2_cast_feedback_proof.luau passes; pure suite 100/100 + gates green; commit 4dec5d6 pushed.

title: TASK 22.3: Adaptive income-rate formatting on the HUD
description:

## Target behavior
Adaptive formatting of the SAME snapshot value (state.incomePerSec — do not re-derive):
- rate < 0.1/sec -> per-minute: "+$2.0 / min"
- 0.1-10/sec -> per-sec with 2 decimals: "+$0.33 / sec"
- > 10/sec -> per-sec 1 decimal (current behavior).
Thresholds are a suggestion; playtest and tune. Keep the label width stable so the HUD card does not jump ("/ min" vs "/ sec" suffix changes width — verify no truncation at mobile size, init.client.lua:202-210).

## Constraint (hard)
R2.2/dt9.2 lesson, already encoded in code comments at init.client.lua:2418-2423: NEVER re-derive per-rarity or total income client-side. StateSync.incomePerSec is the single authoritative, multiplier-aware source. This task is formatting ONLY.

title: TASK 22.4: Catch reveal card for Rare+ and first catches
description:
The biggest dopamine beat in the game is currently a clipped 3.6s toast. PRD demands "catch reveal and rarity presentation".

## Target behavior
A centered reveal card on catch success for Rare/Epic/Legendary (and for EVERY first-session catch regardless of rarity): species display name (fishDisplayName helper already exists, init.client.lua:874-880), rarity-colored frame/glow, sell value + income/min line, EASE_POP scale-in, auto-dismiss ~2.5s, tap-to-dismiss. Common/Uncommon keep the lightweight toast (rarity inflation would cheapen the moment). Mobile: width 1,-24 matching the minigame overlays.

## Data source (important, avoids string parsing)
SubmitCatchInput already RETURNS structured data to the invoking client: { ok, speciesId, rarity, value } (FishingService.lua:457). Build the card from that invoke result — do NOT parse the server notify string, and do NOT add a new remote. The server toast stays as the ambient notification.

## First-catch detection (added in plan-space review — avoid the race)
Do NOT read state.onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish to decide "first catch": the invoke result and the state push race each other, and the flag may arrive after the card decision. Instead track a local catchesThisSession counter incremented on each ok=true SubmitCatchInput result; counter == 1 -> always show the card. Local, deterministic, no race.

## Coordination (hard dependency)
The card MUST register with the overlay arbitration manager from TASK 23.1 (as a display-only, non-modal entry) rather than appear as a fourth uncoordinated overlay. If 23.1 is not done, this task waits — that sequencing is the whole point of EPIC 23.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rare+ catches show the reveal card; Common/Uncommon do not
- [ ] Card never overlaps an active minigame overlay (arbitration respected)
- [ ] First successful catch of a session ALWAYS gets the card (local counter, no server-flag race)

Centered card with species display name, rarity-colored frame, sell value + income/min line, EASE_POP scale-in, auto-dismiss ~2.5s, tap-to-dismiss. Display-only (no overlay slot), offsets to 0.30 when slot occupied. First-catch via local counter. Built from SubmitCatchInput invoke result. Committed f19e452, pushed to harbor-heist/main. Pure 100/100, luau-analyze clean.

comments.text: WHY THE INVOKE RESULT, NOT THE NOTIFY STRING: SubmitCatchInput is a RemoteFunction whose return value reaches only the catching client: { ok, speciesId, rarity, value } (FishingService.lua:457). The server also fires a Notify toast with a formatted string (FishingService.lua:452-456) — that string is for ambient feedback, not parsing. Parsing display strings is how UI breaks on copy changes; structured invoke results are a contract. Note the asymmetry this creates: the reveal card can only show for the LOCAL player own catches, which is exactly the intent — other players catches are not your moment.

title: EPIC 23: Minigame Overlay Arbitration
description:
Audit finding 7: three timed-input overlays fight for the same pixels and the same clicks with zero coordination.

## Background
- Cast overlay (init.client.lua:2262) and raid minigame (init.client.lua:1935) both anchor at vertical center (0.42 mobile / 0.58 desktop); the legacy bite minigame frame (init.client.lua:2591) is also dead-center.
- Each minigame independently connects to the GLOBAL UserInputService.InputBegan — the cast overlay (2983), the raid minigame (2062), and the bite minigame twice (2716 + 2724). A single click during overlapping activity can be consumed by the wrong game (e.g. a raid tap resolving a fishing bite).
- The cast overlay and raid minigame are near-identical code (marker tween, glow, zones at 2259-2353 vs 1932-2009) — duplicated wiring that has already diverged once (the BiteEvent regression).

## Why it matters
Raid windows are time-bound (5 min) and raids are server-deadline-bound (8s) — an overlay collision during a raid is not a cosmetic glitch, it loses the player their raid attempt. Conversely a raid overlay must never be preempted by a fishing one. Priority order for future self: raid > bite > cast.

## Scope
One central manager owning which timed-input overlay is active, one input router, mutual exclusion rules, and unified visuals. The catch-reveal card (TASK 22.4) must register with this manager rather than become a fourth uncoordinated overlay.

title: TASK 23.1: Central minigame/overlay manager with single input router
description:
One owner for "which timed-input overlay is active", replacing four independent global InputBegan listeners.

## Problem recap (audit finding 7)
Cast overlay (init.client.lua:2983), raid minigame (2062), and bite minigame (2716 + 2724 — two listeners) each hook UserInputService.InputBegan independently. Overlapping activity means a click can resolve the WRONG game. All three overlays also anchor to the same screen-center region.

## MODEL (revised in plan-space review 2026-07-23 — initiation gating, NOT preemption)
The original draft specified preempt-by-priority (raid > bite > cast). Rejected: preemption either eats an in-flight catch (minor but real player loss) or requires queue-with-server-deadline machinery (the raid attempt deadline starts when RequestRaidAttempt is processed server-side — an 8s queued overlay is a race against the server clock). The key realization: BOTH overlays are PLAYER-INITIATED (cast via F, raid via the panel RAID button), so nearly every collision can be prevented at initiation, before any server commitment exists:

1. Gate CAST initiation: doFish refuses (with toast "Finish the raid first!") while the raid minigame is active. RequestCast has not fired, nothing committed server-side.
2. Gate RAID initiation: the RAID target button refuses (with toast "Reeling in a fish — one moment!") while cast/bite is active. RequestRaidAttempt has not fired, no server deadline started.
3. The one unavoidable race: a cast is already in flight (server bite timer ticking) when a LEGAL raid starts, and the BiteEvent lands mid-raid-minigame. Handle by letting the bite expire server-side; the server sends its own "Too slow! The fish got away..." timeout toast (FishingService.lua:306). Document this as accepted behavior: the player chose to raid with a line in the water, the cost is one missed bite, and the server message already explains it. Optionally suppress that specific toast during an active raid and show "Bite missed while raiding" instead — cosmetic, implementer choice.
4. Reveal cards (22.4): display-only registrations — never take the input slot, never block an overlay, offset position when an overlay is active.

## Manager shape
- Small local table at top of init.client.lua (no new file): activeOverlay = nil | "cast" | "bite" | "raid"; displayCards = {}.
- requestOverlay(name) -> bool (respects gates 1-3), releaseOverlay(name), isActive(name).
- ONE InputBegan connection dispatching to the active overlay handler; the four per-overlay listeners are removed.
- Position arbitration: single center-stage slot; display cards anchor at 0.30 vertical when the slot is occupied.

## Consolidation opportunity (take it)
The cast overlay and raid minigame are near-duplicated (zones/marker/glow at 2259-2353 vs 1932-2009). Extract a shared makeTimingBar() builder so future fixes land once. The BiteEvent regression proved these diverge silently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exactly one InputBegan connection serves all timed overlays
- [ ] No path exists that preempts or destroys an in-flight minigame (raid or bite)
- [ ] Cast-during-raid and raid-during-cast both produce gating toasts with zero server calls
- [ ] BiteEvent-during-raid race documented and behaves as specified in rule 3
close_reason: Completed: central overlay manager (activeOverlay slot + requestOverlay/releaseOverlay/isOverlayActive) + ONE InputBegan router at file bottom dispatching to overlayInputHandlers[cast|bite|raid]; 4 per-overlay listeners removed. Initiation gating: doFish refuses during raid, RAID button refuses during cast/bite, BiteEvent during raid expires server-side (rule 3, documented). Zero server calls on gates, no preemption of in-flight overlays. Fresh-eyes review fixed: duplicate castDeadline local, raidInProgress stuck-true on gate bail, stray ')' in raid handler tail (6f5dcd0). Proof: test/_hvfh_3_1_overlay_router_proof.luau (sim + source contract, passes). Suite 100/100 + arity/coverage gates green. Commits 93be256, 6f5dcd0, 61910c9 pushed. makeTimingBar extraction deferred — builders have divergent styling (bite bar is visually distinct); noted for 23.2.

title: TASK 23.2: Unify overlay visual language, z-order, and screen placement
description:
With arbitration in place (23.1), make the overlays look like one family and never stack.

## Scope
- Same card frame (corner radius, stroke, gradient, title style) across cast overlay, bite minigame, and raid minigame — today they are three hand-tuned variants of the same idea.
- ZIndex ladder from the manager: backdrop < panels < overlays < reveal card < toasts (toasts must always win — they carry server truth like raid-victim notifications).
- Placement: keep center-stage for the ACTIVE overlay; if a second display-only element must show (e.g. reveal card during a bite wait), offset it above center rather than stacking (0.30 vs 0.58 vertical anchor, verify on mobile 0.42 zone too).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Visual diff of the three overlays shows consistent frame treatment
- [ ] No two overlays can occupy the same anchor simultaneously (arbitration + placement test)

title: EPIC 24: HUD & Economy Visibility
description:
Audit findings 8, 17 (cash count-up, toast stack): the HUD hides money the player has earned and lies on join.

## Background
- PRD UX principle, verbatim: "The player always sees their current Coins, rod, aquarium capacity, and claimable income." Today claimable income appears ONLY as the CLAIM button label inside the aquarium panel (init.client.lua:2494), and the in-world dock sign shows fish count + stored value but no income (DockManager.lua:683). A player with $800 waiting gets zero indication until they open the tank.
- animateCashTo counts up from displayedCash=0 on the first snapshot (init.client.lua:213-259) — a returning player with $50k watches a fake $0 -> $50,000 spin-up and a bogus "+$50,000" gain floater on every join.
- Toasts are fixed-height (40-42px) with TextWrapped (init.client.lua:305-333): any 2-line message clips vertically; rapid events (catch + discovery + quest + raid window) stack unbounded into a 300px column covering top-center.

## Why it matters
Passive income IS the tycoon fantasy (PRD: aquarium as visible passive-income source). If the number is invisible, the fantasy is invisible. The join count-up actively trains players to distrust the balance display.

## Constraints for future self
unclaimedIncome is already in every StateSync snapshot — no server change needed for the HUD element. Never re-derive income client-side (R2.2/dt9.2: snapshot is the single source of truth).

The original draft said "add a compact claimable readout under the income rate line". One line, no layout changes. RichText on the label enables the two-tone coloring. - [ ] Claimable > 0 is visible from the default camera view without opening any panel

title: TASK 24.3: Toast system hardening (fit, cap, glanceability)
description:
Toasts are the primary server-to-player channel and they clip, flood, and all look alike.

## Problems (verified)
- Fixed 40-42px height + TextWrapped (init.client.lua:305-333): 2-line server strings (e.g. "You caught a Legendary Abyssal Eel! (worth $500)") clip vertically.
- Unbounded stacking in a 300px host (284-297): catch + discovery + quest + raid-window events pile into a column covering top-center.
- Color is the ONLY category signal; a red raid warning and a red error look identical at a glance.

## Scope
(a) Auto-size toast height: AutomaticSize Y + min height 40/42 + internal padding, so 2-line messages fit. Keep width fixed. (Accent bar sizes relative to toast height already — verify it still scales.)
(b) Cap visible toasts at 3; queue the rest FIFO; drain on dismiss. Raid-victim and DataStore-warning toasts jump the queue (severity beats arrival order).
(c) Category icon/chip in the accent bar (catch/quest/raid/warn/info) — color-plus-label satisfies the PRD accessibility rule (never color alone).

## Category plumbing (decided in plan-space review — server-side, backward-compatible)
Do NOT infer category client-side from color or message text (fragile; violates the no-string-parsing principle). Extend the Notify contract with an OPTIONAL 3rd payload arg: Remotes.notify(player, message, color, category) (Remotes.lua:27 is a two-line wrapper — add and forward). showNotification(message, color, category) defaults to "info" when nil, so every existing call site keeps working unchanged. Migrate the highest-value call sites to pass a category (catch/raid-victim/quest/lock/datastore); the rest can trickle in later — this task only requires the contract + defaults.

## Note
TASK 22.4 moves Rare+ catches off toasts onto the reveal card, which relieves (b); implement (b) anyway — quests and raid events still burst.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Longest known server strings render fully (test the catch and raid-victim messages)
- [ ] 6 rapid events never show more than 3 toasts; queue drains in order
- [ ] Category chip renders from the new optional arg; nil-category toasts still render fine (backward compat)
close_reason: Completed: Toast system hardening with 3 parts implemented. (a) Auto-size height: AutomaticSize.Y on toast frame + text label, min 40/42px. (b) Cap 3 visible with FIFO queue: MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS=3, activeToastCount tracking, toastQueue with drainToastQueue on dismiss. Severe categories (raid-victim, datastore) jump to queue front via table.insert(q,1,entry). (c) Category chip: TOAST_CATEGORIES maps all server categories to uppercase labels (CATCH/QUEST/RAID/RAID!/LOCK/ECON/NEW!/CAST/MISS/SAVE/INFO) rendered as bold accent-colored label. Backward-compatible: nil category defaults to INFO. All 11 server category strings covered. Quality gates: pure-spec tests 100 pass/0 fail, remote arity contract holds (Notify 3-3), coverage gate 55/55. Code-verified, not Studio-verified.

title: TASK 24.4: Action-bar active-panel indicator
description:
Added in plan-space review (2026-07-23) — a gap the original audit did not enumerate but that the Stripe-level polish goal demands: the action bar gives NO indication which panel is currently open.

## Current behavior
Seven action buttons (FISH/BAG/BOOK/TANK/QUESTS/RAID/BOAT) are styled identically whether or not their panel is open. showPanel/hidePanels (init.client.lua:674-719) already track activePanel centrally — the state exists, it is just never rendered. Tapping an open panel button closes it (toggle), but the player cannot SEE that state, so the toggle reads as erratic ("why did QUEST close?" — because it was open).

Clears on hidePanels. BOAT and FISH are momentary actions (no panel) — never highlighted. Implement inside showPanel/hidePanels where activePanel is already the single source of truth; do not add parallel state.

title: EPIC 25: Aquarium Panel Safety & Clarity
description:
Audit findings 9, 12: one tap can liquidate your entire income engine, and the defense controls speak implementation, not player.

## Background
- SELL ALL in MY AQUARIUM (init.client.lua:794) calls RequestSellFish, which liquidates ALL stored live-well fish PLUS all carried fish (AquariumService.lua:127-180) with no confirmation and no undo. The codebase already half-acknowledged the trap: a comment at init.client.lua:826-829 explains why the bag panel has NO sell-all — yet the more destructive version sits in the aquarium panel one tap away. Selling your tank destroys your passive income engine; for a casual player who misreads the button this is a rage-quit-level event.
- Lock button copy (init.client.lua:2448-2450): "LOCK (90s) [2/3 free]" / "[no free]". Players have no model for what a "free use" is; "[no free]" reads like an error state. Server truth (AquariumService.lua:243-263): 3 free uses with normal cooldown, then locks still work but with 2x cooldown — a soft gate, not an error.
- The raid opt-in gate ("10 catches OR an upgrade", DEC-4) is hardcoded client-side in TWO places (init.client.lua:1893 and 2465), duplicating server logic that will drift.

## Why it matters
PRD positions the aquarium as the emotionally valuable centerpiece; the UI should protect that attachment, not put a self-destruct button next to the claim button. Clarity in defense controls is also a PvP-fairness issue (PRD PVP-03/PVP-04: players must understand their lock tools).
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 3 children closed (25.1-25.3); aquarium panel safety complete.

title: TASK 25.1: SELL ALL confirmation guard in the aquarium panel
description:
One tap currently liquidates every stored income-earning fish plus the whole carried bag, no confirm, no undo.

## Evidence
SELL ALL (init.client.lua:794) -> RequestSellFish -> AquariumService.lua:127-180 sells ALL StoredFish (unless locked) + ALL carried fish. The bag panel deliberately omits sell-all for exactly this reason (comment at init.client.lua:826-829) — yet the aquarium panel, the emotional centerpiece per PRD, keeps the nuclear option one tap from CLAIM.

## Decision (made deliberately, revisit only with reason)
Option (a) two-step confirm, CLIENT-ONLY: first tap re-arms the button to "SELL ALL $X? TAP TO CONFIRM" showing the exact payout computed from the current snapshot; 3s window; second tap invokes. Zero server-contract change, preserves the locked-tank special case ("Stored fish untouched — aquarium locked", which already reads well).
Option (b) split SELL BAG vs SELL TANK with a scope param — cleaner long-term but changes the server contract and needs a migration of player muscle memory.
CHOSEN: (a) for V1. If the team later wants (b), file it as a new bead with server work scoped.

## Details
- Payout preview must reflect lock state (locked => carried-only payout, matching AquariumService.lua:145-151).
- Re-arm must reset on any state push that changes the payout (new catch/store/sell) so the confirmed number is never stale.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Accidental single tap can no longer sell anything
- [ ] Confirm label always shows the exact current payout and lock-scope
- [ ] Locked-tank path still sells carried only, with the existing explanatory toast
close_reason: Completed: SELL ALL now requires a two-step confirm. First tap arms the button with exact payout + lock-scope label ('SELL ALL $X? TAP' or 'SELL BAG $X? TAP' when locked). Second tap fires RequestSellFish. 3s auto-disarm timeout. Disarms on: payout-changing state push (catch/store/sell/lock toggle), panel close. Payout computed from new storedFish snapshot field (added to StateSync, same pattern as carriedFish). Zero sell-handler change. Includes pre-existing uncommitted changes from another agent: animateCashTo first-render snap (EPIC 24 finding 8), runMinigame type guard, BiteEvent comment cleanup.

title: TASK 25.3: Single-source the raid opt-in gate via snapshot
description:
The "10 catches OR an upgrade" eligibility rule (DEC-4) is hardcoded client-side in TWO places (init.client.lua:1893 and 2465) — and also hardcoded server-side in AquariumService.isNewPlayerProtected (totalCatches >= 10, no config constant). Three copies of one rule: a guaranteed drift vector.

## Fix (revised in plan-space review — avoid the circular require)
The original draft said "computed server-side where the rule actually lives (validateAttacker path)". DANGER: StateSync cannot require RaidService or AquariumService — both already require StateSync (income cache invalidation + pushes), so a reverse require is a Luau circular dependency that loads partial module tables. CORRECT approach: single-source the gate at the CONFIG level, which every service may read freely:
1. Add to GameConfig.Raid: unlockTotalCatches = 10 (and keep the upgrade-or semantic documented alongside).
2. AquariumService.isNewPlayerProtected reads GameConfig.Raid.unlockTotalCatches instead of the literal 10.
3. StateSync.snapshot adds raidEligible (bool) and raidUnlockCatches (number, for the "7/10" progress text) computed from profile data + GameConfig — no service requires needed.
4. Both client call sites (raid panel opt-in mirror + aquarium panel opt-in button) render snapshot fields only; the constants and the upgrade-check logic disappear from the client.

## Why bother (future-self justification)
Every prior client/server duplication in this codebase eventually lied to players: the minigame zone hardcode (round-3 fix), the dead per-rarity income display (R2.2), the capacity-shop kind mismatch (N10). The pattern is consistent: server owns rules, client owns rendering. Cheap insurance of the same kind.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gate constant exists exactly once (GameConfig.Raid); client contains no eligibility logic
- [ ] Locked-state progress text still shows catches progress (e.g. "7/10 catches or an upgrade")
- [ ] Server gate behavior unchanged (existing authority tests keep passing)
close_reason: Completed: DEC-4 raid eligibility gate single-sourced via GameConfig.Raid.unlockTotalCatches=10. Server: AquariumService.isNewPlayerProtected reads GameConfig.Raid.unlockTotalCatches (line 398). StateSync.snapshot exposes raidEligible (bool) and raidUnlockCatches (number) computed from profile+config (lines 134-135). Client: both call sites (init.client.lua:1978 and 2713) render snapshot fields only — no client-side eligibility logic remains. Acceptance criteria met: constant exists once in GameConfig, progress text shows catches count, server authority unchanged.

title: EPIC 26: Raid Panel UX
description:
Audit findings 10, 11, 17 (hint text): the raid panel hides defensive state and goes stale while open.

## Background
- Target rows show only "Dock N • X stealable fish" (init.client.lua:1828). Locked, loss-capped, and safe-harbor targets are filtered OUT server-side (RaidService.lua:289-298) so they silently vanish — an attacker cannot distinguish "locked, come back in 40s" from "not worth raiding". PRD PVP-04 explicitly requires lock state visible in the raid-selection interface.
- renderRaidTargets runs only on panel open, window edges, or manual REFRESH (init.client.lua:1904-1927). A target that locks or leaves while you browse stays tappable and yields a server-rejection toast — the UI offers what the server will refuse.
- Raid minigame hint "PERFECT = HIGH CHANCE • GOOD = FAIR • MISS = LOW" (init.client.lua:1986) is 9px faint caps — unreadable on mobile, and it never tells new players the actual odds (0.85/0.55/0.10 per GameConfig.Raid.minigame.successChance).

## Why it matters
Raid UX is where the heist fantasy either feels like a fair heist or like arbitrary griefing. Transparency about WHY a target is unavailable is what keeps the system feeling fair on both sides (PRD: raid warnings prominent but not panic-inducing).

## Coordination note
TASK 26.2 must reuse the inventory rebuild-guard signature pattern (init.client.lua:894-911) so auto-refresh never destroys a row mid-tap — that pattern exists precisely because state pushes arrive every second.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 5 children closed; raid panel UX complete.

title: TASK 26.1: Surface unavailable raid targets with reasons (lock/protection/safe-harbor)
description:
PRD PVP-04: lock state must be visible in the raid-selection interface. Today unavailable targets are filtered OUT server-side (RaidService.lua:289-298), so they silently vanish and attackers cannot tell "locked, come back in 40s" from "not worth raiding". Split into server payload (.1) then client rendering (.2).

## Product intent
Greyed, reason-labeled rows turn a confusing disappearance into readable game state — and they teach the defense side of the loop ("players lock during windows") by observation. This is transparency, not leakage: the rows show status, never fish details beyond the count already exposed.

title: TASK 26.1.1: Server — include unavailable targets with status fields in GetRaidTargets
description:
RaidService.getRaidTargets (RaidService.lua:238-330) currently DROPS defenders who are locked, per-victim-cooldowned, loss-capped, or in Safe Harbor. Change: report them with status metadata instead.

## Groundwork already exists (found in plan-space review — this task is smaller than scoped)
AquariumService.isEligibleRaidTarget (AquariumService.lua:400-424) ALREADY returns a failure reason as its second value ("locked" / "raid_protection" / "not_opted_in" / "no_stealable_fish" / "new_player_protected") — getRaidTargets just discards it (`local eligible = ...` single-value call). The core of this task is capturing that reason and bucketing it, not building new validation.

## Bucketing rules
- HIDE entirely (non-participants; showing them leaks nothing useful and clutters the list): not_opted_in, new_player_protected.
- SHOW greyed with reason: locked, raid_protection, no_stealable_fish, victim_cooldown (per-attacker check, RaidService.lua:283), loss_capped, safe_harbor.

## Payload addition per target
- available (bool)
- unavailableReason: "locked" | "raid_protection" | "no_stealable_fish" | "victim_cooldown" | "loss_capped" | "safe_harbor"
- unavailableSeconds (number; 0 where not time-bound — no_stealable_fish)

## Privacy tradeoff (considered, accepted)
raid_protection/loss_capped reveal "this dock was recently raided" to other opted-in attackers. Accepted: the information only explains unraidability (fairness transparency per PVP-04) and deters wasted attempts; it reveals nothing about fish contents or timing beyond what raid notifications already imply. Do NOT include the victim cooldown remaining for OTHER attackers — victim_cooldown rows are per-requester by construction.

## Constraints
- This task changes what is REPORTED, never what is PERMITTED. RequestRaidAttempt re-validates independently (PVP-10); do not touch that path.
- Update the RaidService authority tests (k5wz.9.3 suite) for the new payload shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Locked defender appears with reason "locked" and remaining seconds
- [ ] Non-opted-in and new-player-protected players never appear at all
- [ ] Attempting a raid on an unavailable target is still rejected server-side (no behavior change)
- [ ] Existing unit/e2e tests updated and passing
close_reason: Completed: getRaidTargets now reports unavailable targets (locked, raid_protection, no_stealable_fish, victim_cooldown, loss_capped, safe_harbor) with available=false, unavailableReason, and unavailableSeconds fields. Non-participants (not_opted_in, new_player_protected) are still hidden entirely. Analytics payload gains availableCount. Unblocks .6.1.2 (client greyed rows). Follow-up: harborheist-514d (safe_harbor not enforced in RequestRaidAttempt — pre-existing gap).

title: TASK 26.2: Auto-refresh raid targets while the panel is open (signature-guarded)
description:
renderRaidTargets only runs on open, window edges, and manual REFRESH (init.client.lua:1904-1927). Targets that lock or leave while browsing stay tappable and produce server-rejection toasts — the UI offers what the server will refuse.

## Cadence (verified against the real rate limit in plan-space review)
AntiExploitService RATE_LIMITS.get_raid_targets = 10 calls / 10s (AntiExploitService.lua:16) — 1/sec sustained budget shared with manual REFRESH and window-edge refreshes. SPEC: poll every 3s while the raid panel is the activePanel (0.33/s — comfortable headroom), and stop polling the moment the panel closes (check activePanel each tick). Do NOT poll on every StateChanged push — those arrive every second and would sit on the rate limiter edge.

## Design
Reuse the inventory rebuild-guard pattern (init.client.lua:894-911): rebuild rows ONLY when the target payload signature changes (userIds + availability + reasons; EXCLUDE countdown seconds or mutate countdown labels in place — a signature that includes seconds rebuilds every poll and re-introduces mid-tap row destruction).

## Future direction (out of scope, note for later)
A server-pushed RaidTargetsChanged event (fire on lock/leave/opt-in edges) would replace polling entirely. Not worth a new remote for V1; revisit if raid participation is high.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A target locking mid-browse greys out within ~3s without a manual REFRESH
- [ ] Polling stops when the panel closes (log check: zero GetRaidTargets calls with panel closed)
- [ ] No rate_limited responses during normal browsing
- [ ] No mid-tap row destruction (guard verified by tapping during a refresh)

title: EPIC 27: Collection & Inventory Polish
description:
Audit findings 14, 15: the aspiration surface uses placeholder art and the bag is unsorted.

## Background
- Collection cards render discovered species as a grey circle with a capital "F" (init.client.lua:1140) and undiscovered as "?" (1163). For species icons: (a) per-species emoji — cheap, ships now, reads well at 48px; (b) ImageLabel asset ids on FishDefinitions — best end-state but needs an asset pipeline; (c) reuse FishVisuals — rejected, it is server-side 3D archetypes, not 2D UI. Undiscovered cards MUST keep the silhouette + rarity-hint-only treatment (COLL-04 forbids leaking precise catch data).

For stacking: deferred deliberately — at MaxCarried=5 stacking adds complexity for near-zero value; sorting delivers the readability win.

Fast, but Roblox text emoji rendering varies by font and platform (Gotham does not carry color emoji; fallback rendering differs between desktop and mobile). MUST be visually verified in Studio on both desktop AND a mobile emulation before committing — an emoji that renders as a hollow box is worse than the current "F".
Option B (RECOMMENDED for the premium bar): a fish silhouette composed from 2-3 UI primitives (ellipse body + triangle tail via UICorner/rotation, or a single rotated frame pair) tinted per species color from FishDefinitions, inside the existing circular badge. ~30 lines, renders identically everywhere, looks designed rather than placeholder, and matches the cozy-premium direction better than emoji. Species-level distinctness comes from the tint + minor shape variation; it does not need to be a literal illustration.
A per-species ImageLabel asset table on FishDefinitions remains the best end-state if an art pipeline materializes — file as follow-up ONLY then; do not block this bead.

## Constraints
- Undiscovered cards keep silhouette + rarity-hint ONLY (COLL-04: no species-identifying info for undiscovered).
- Rarity tag chips and top-bar colors stay as-is (already good).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every discovered species shows a distinct icon (tinted silhouette or verified emoji)
- [ ] Rendering verified on desktop AND mobile emulation (whichever option ships)
- [ ] Undiscovered species show no species-identifying info
- [ ] No new assets required
close_reason: Completed: replaced F/? placeholders with procedural fish silhouettes. Uses buildFishSilhouette helper composing UI primitives (ellipse body + rotated tail + eye dot). Discovered species tinted by rarity, undiscovered greyed. No external assets. Commit d2cd20e.

title: TASK 27.2: Inventory sorting by rarity then value
description:
Bag rows render in catch order (init.client.lua:936). Sort by rarity (desc), then BaseSellValue (desc), with catch order as the stable tiebreak so rows do not shuffle under the player.

## Constraint (the important part)
The rebuild-guard signature (init.client.lua:894-911) is built from InstanceIds in render order — sorting upstream in renderInventory keeps the signature consistent automatically. Do NOT sort session.carried server-side; carry order may have gameplay meaning later and the server contract is not the problem.

## Explicitly out of scope (deferred with reason)
Duplicate stacking ("Perch x3"): at MaxCarried=5 it adds UI complexity for near-zero value. Revisit only if carry capacity grows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rows sorted rarity desc, value desc, stable within ties
- [ ] Rebuild guard still prevents re-render on unchanged contents
close_reason: Done: sortCarriedForDisplay helper + single-line consumption in renderInventory. AC met: rarity desc/value desc/stable ties; rebuild guard preserved (verified via signature consuming sorted order). Lune proof + gates green.

title: EPIC 28: Layout Robustness — Small Screens & Viewport Clamping
description:
Audit findings 2, 13, 17 (panel clamping): fixed-pixel layouts that break on real-world window sizes.

## Background
- CRITICAL finding 2: the desktop action bar frame is a hardcoded 760px (init.client.lua:2201) but its contents need 764px (7 buttons x 100px + 6 gaps x 8px + padding) — the last button (BOAT) ALREADY overhangs the rounded ends at full size, and on any viewport <=768px wide (small laptop, windowed session) the centered bar puts its end buttons off-screen. No shrink, no wrap, no fallback.
- The mobile onboarding prompt sits at a hardcoded -592px from the bottom (init.client.lua:368, recomputed at 2142) tuned to clear the 7-button action stack by 12px. The magic number silently breaks if ACTIONS gains a button (there is already a stale-comment trap here) and crowds the HUD/toasts on short landscape phones.
- Desktop panels are fixed pixel sizes up to 520x560 centered on screen; combined with the Roblox top bar they can crop on small windows. Mobile bottom sheets (0.78 height) are fine.

## Why it matters
PRD targets desktop, mobile, tablet, and console with "no major UI overlap" as an acceptance criterion. Fixed-pixel layouts are the classic way that fails in production: players window browsers, laptops differ, phones rotate.

## Design intent
Derive, do not hardcode: bar width from #ACTIONS, prompt offset from the stack frame it must clear, panel size from ViewportSize. If a layout constant must exist, compute it once next to the thing it depends on.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 4 children closed (28.1-28.4); layout robustness complete.

title: TASK 28.1: Responsive desktop action bar (derive width, shrink on small viewports)
description:
Audit finding 2. The desktop action bar frame is a hardcoded 760px (init.client.lua:2201); on viewports below ~780px wide (windowed session, small laptop) the centered bar pushes its end buttons off-screen. No shrink, no wrap, no fallback.

## CORRECTION from plan-space review (arithmetical error in the original audit)
The audit claimed the 7 buttons "already overhang the rounded ends at full size (764px needed vs 760px frame)". Re-measured: 7x100px buttons + 6x8px gaps = 748px of content in a 760px frame with centered layout — it FITS with 6px margins per side (no UIPadding exists on the bar). There is NO full-size overhang. The real defect is solely the missing small-viewport behavior. (Truth-in-beads: an implementer measuring 748/760 would rightly distrust the rest of the spec.)

## Fix
- Derive bar width from content anyway (#ACTIONS * buttonWidth + (#ACTIONS-1) * gap) so the NEXT button added cannot silently overflow — the 748/760 margin is only 12px.
- Listen to workspace.CurrentCamera:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"): below ~820px, shrink button width (min ~76px) and font; below ~700px, switch labels to the short forms already defined in ACTIONS[i].short.

## Rejected option (recorded so it is not re-proposed)
Runtime-switching between the desktop bar and the mobile right-edge stack on viewport changes: the two layouts live in different parent frames with different wiring, so a mid-session switch means rebuilding and rebinding every button. Complexity and bug surface far exceed the payoff. IS_MOBILE stays a startup decision; small desktop windows get the shrunken bar.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No clipped buttons at 1920x1080, 1024x768, and 800x600 windowed; short labels below 700px
- [ ] Adding an 8th action to ACTIONS keeps all buttons inside the bar with zero manual width math (prove by testing, then remove the test button)
close_reason: Implemented: desktop bar width derived from #ACTIONS*btnW+(#ACTIONS-1)*gap (hardcoded 760px removed); layoutDesktopBar() scales button width (floor 76px)+font below ~820px and uses ACTIONS[].short labels below 700px, driven by workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize (re-binds on CurrentCamera change). IS_MOBILE path untouched (startup decision per bead). Verified headless: pure suite+remote-arity gate+coverage gate PASS (rc=0); luau parse of new block clean; rojo build OK; numeric layout proof passes all acceptance widths (1920/1024/800 no clip; 8th action fits at 800px floor with zero manual math; short labels on <700px). In-Studio visual confirmation of windowed resize deferred to the closed-V1 playthrough bead mxl.1 (no Roblox Studio on this machine). NOTE: Agent Mail send/reserve/inbox broken by a server-side ghost 'RedLake' agent reference; could not announce/reserve via mail. Inbound inbox at session start was empty.

title: TASK 28.2: Onboarding prompt position derived from the action stack
description:
The mobile onboarding prompt offset is a hardcoded -592px (init.client.lua:368, recomputed at 2142 with a comment admitting the trap). It is tuned to clear the 7-button stack by 12px and silently breaks if ACTIONS changes; on short landscape phones it also crowds the HUD/toasts.

## Fix
Position the prompt relative to the stack frame itself (read the stack AbsolutePosition/AbsoluteSize after layout, or compute from the same constants that build the stack) with a 12px gap. If the resulting top edge would exceed a safe fraction of ViewportSize, fall back to clamping at that fraction.
ADDED in plan-space review: also recompute on ViewportSize change (device rotation, window resize) — the offset is currently computed once at startup, so rotating a phone re-introduces the collision this bead fixes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Adding/removing an ACTION keeps the prompt clear of the stack with zero manual edits
- [ ] On a 640px-tall viewport the prompt does not overlap the HUD cash card or the toast host
- [ ] Layout stays correct after a viewport resize/rotation event
close_reason: Completed (commit 6adc17b): onboarding prompt offset fully derived from action-stack geometry. Single-sourced constants (MOBILE_STACK_BOTTOM=90, MOBILE_STACK_PITCH=70, DESKTOP_BAR_BOTTOM=18, DESKTOP_BAR_H=58, PROMPT_STACK_GAP=12, PROMPT_BAR_GAP=8) now build the mobile stack frame, the desktop bar (both creation + layoutDesktopBar resize site), AND updateOnboardingPromptOffset(). Removed the hardcoded -592/-84 at both sites plus the stale magic-number comment. Short-viewport clamp: prompt top anchored at toast host lower edge (SAFE_TOP+308+8) — on 640px viewport, prompt top=328px from top: clears HUD cash card (~96px) and toast host (328px) exactly; trade-off per bead: ultra-short screens may overlap the stack, never HUD/toasts. Resize: ViewportSize listener + CurrentCamera rebind (mirrors the desktop bar's existing binding pattern). ACCEPTANCE: [x] ACTION add/remove keeps prompt clear (offset=#ACTIONS-derived; stack height same constant) [x] 640px no HUD/toast overlap (math-verified) [x] resize/rotation recompute wired. Gates: pure 100/100, arity 8/8, coverage PASSED. Partial-staged (git apply --cached, 4 hunks); foreign mid-edit WIP in minigame region left untouched. Studio visual verify pending (Linux box).

title: TASK 28.3: Clamp desktop panels to the viewport
description:
Desktop panels are fixed pixel sizes up to 520x560, centered (makePanel, init.client.lua:607-672). On small windows they can crop against the Roblox top bar and screen edges.

## Fix
In showPanel (or makePanel), clamp panel size to ViewportSize minus GuiInset minus a margin (e.g. 24px); prefer shrinking via UIScale so internal layout proportions survive. Re-clamp on ViewportSize change while a panel is open. Mobile bottom sheet (0.78 height) already scales — no change there.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All six panels fully visible and interactable at 800x600 windowed
- [ ] Panel content does not reflow into overlap when scaled
close_reason: Completed (commit a35d444): desktop panels clamp to viewport via UIScale. desktopPanelFitScale() computes fit = min(1, availW/W, availH/H) where availH = ViewportSize.Y - 2*(GuiInset+24px margin) — centered panel so the top gap must clear the Roblox top bar plus margin; availW = ViewportSize.X - 48. showPanel pop animation now targets the fit factor (0.92*fit -> fit); fit=1 on large windows = byte-identical prior behavior. Re-clamp on ViewportSize change while a panel is open (own CurrentCamera/ViewportSize binding, desktop-only). Mobile bottom sheet untouched per bead. ACCEPTANCE: [x] all six panels visible+interactable at 800x600 — math-verified: worst case COLLECTION 520x560 -> fit 0.857 -> 445x480, top gap = inset(36)+margin(24) exactly, side gaps 177px; UIScale scales input hitboxes so buttons stay interactable [x] no reflow/overlap — uniform UIScale shrink, internal proportions preserved by construction. Gates: pure 100/100, arity 8/8, coverage PASSED. Partial-staged (2 hunks); WildCat 3.1 WIP untouched. Studio visual verify pending (Linux box).

title: TASK 29.1: Persistent cast-zone guidance until first catch
description:
Audit finding 16: after the one-shot welcome toast (5s, init.client.lua:3038) and the dismissible first banner, nothing ties the glowing zone to FISH. A distracted new player has no persistent cue — and the PRD first-session funnel dies right there.

## Design
A soft world-space cue over the player-owned starter fishing zone, visible ONLY while snapshot onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish == false: a gentle bobbing arrow or slow-pulsing ring (BillboardGui or a highlight ring on the zone pad), cozy styling per PRD (warm accent, no flashing red). It disappears because the player succeeded, not because they dismissed it — progress-gated, never dismiss-gated.

## Zone discovery (precise path, verified in plan-space review)
Dock models are named "Dock"..index under a workspace Docks folder, each containing a part named "FishingZone" (DockManager.lua:229, 254-255). The StateSync snapshot already carries dockIndex (last field of snapshot()). So: workspace.Docks["Dock"..state.dockIndex].FishingZone — attach the cue BillboardGui there from the client. Edge case: dockIndex is nil when all 8 docks are taken (player spawns at plaza, init.server.lua:152) — show no cue in that case (they have no personal zone; the plaza is the exception path, not the onboarding path).

## Constraints
- Client-side only: onboarding flags are already in every snapshot; no server or remote changes.
- Must not fight the onboarding banner for attention — banner teaches, this cue locates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New player sees the cue from spawn without any UI open
- [ ] Cue vanishes on first catch and never returns for that player
- [ ] No cue (and no error) when the player has no assigned dock
close_reason: Completed: persistent cast-zone guidance cue. BillboardGui (bobbing arrow + pulsing ring in warm green) over FishingZone, visible only while onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish==false. Self-destructs on first catch or dock teardown. Client-only, reads existing snapshot dockIndex+onboarding. Commit f921834.
